records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'queued' field uses timezone.now() as a dataclass default, which is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource instance forever reports the server's import timestamp. Any consumer relying on 'queued' for staleness/dedup logic (the field exists specifically to record queueing time) gets a wrong, frozen timestamp; worse, the field is never read anywhere in this diff, making it dead payload that also triggers the datetime serialization failure in the Celery path — it should be deleted or computed in __post_init__.
records.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). In a dataclass, that expression is evaluated at class definition/module import time, so all instances will share the same frozen timestamp unless `default_factory=timezone.now` is used. Also, `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, and that dict (including `queued` as a `datetime`) is passed into Celery kwargs via `assignment_source.to_dict()` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)`, which can cause serialization i

records.issue_text: [BUG] AssignmentSource.to_dict() puts a raw datetime and an int integration_id into Celery task kwargs, and from_dict() reconstructs with cls(**input_dict) with no type coercion, so after a JSON-serializing broker round-trip queued arrives as a string and integration_id arrives as a string, and the cycle-prevention check `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` in issues.py compares str vs int and always evaluates False, re-enabling the exact sync loop this diff was written to prevent. With a JSON broker (Celery's default), sync_assignee_outbound deserializes assignment_source_dict with integration_id="123"; should_sync('outbound_assignee', source) at issues.py:389 fails the equality check and proceeds to call sync_assignee_outbound on the same integration that originated the change, producing the cross-system assignment ping-pong loop the diff's comment says it prevents.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition time, so every AssignmentSource built via from_integration (and every reconstructed-from-dict instance that omits queued) shares one frozen import-time timestamp rather than the per-enqueue time the field name promises.
